SQL Injection.explanation:
The /search route takes the `q` value straight from the query string and hands it to search_users() in the service layer, which forwards it unchanged to search_users_by_name() in the data layer. There the value is concatenated directly into a SQL string, which is then executed.

Because the value becomes part of the statement rather than a parameter to it, an attacker controls SQL syntax, not just data. A crafted `q` can close the LIKE clause and append conditions or a UNION, letting them read rows the query was never meant to return -- including other users' records.

default.explanation: Mock response: untrusted input reaches a sensitive operation along the call chain shown above, without a protection being found on the way.

SQL Injection.suggested_fix: Replace the concatenated string in search_users_by_name() with a parameterized query: pass "... WHERE name LIKE ?" and bind f"%{name}%" as a parameter, so the value can never alter the statement. Keep the fix in the data layer rather than escaping in routes/search.py, so every caller is covered; validating the input at the route is worth adding as well, but it is not the fix.
